title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Brooklyn-campus places for research, making, viewing student work, reflection, and informal time between classes.

cards.title: Pratt Institute Brooklyn Campus Library
cards.subtitle: 200 Willoughby Avenue
cards.notes: Set up at a table for research, then use the collection, scanners, printing, research help, or equipment-loan services for a project.
cards.short_summary: A landmark campus library supporting research and studio work.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt identifies its Brooklyn Campus Library as a resource-rich environment for creative teaching and learning, with collections, research support, scanning, printing, and equipment loan.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current visitor guide, hours, and borrowing policies before arriving.

cards.title: Pratt Student Union
cards.subtitle: Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Use the available tables and work spaces for a study session or to meet classmates before moving on to another campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A campus work-space option outside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt states that the Brooklyn campus Student Union has tables and work spaces available for studying.
cards.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions by Parents — Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: Confirm building access and any event-related room changes with Pratt before visiting.

cards.title: Pratt Institute Sculpture Park
cards.subtitle: Across the 25-acre Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Take a slow loop through the lawns and use the Sculpture Park Guide to identify works; the exhibition changes over time.
cards.short_summary: An evolving outdoor collection of more than 70 sculptures.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says its Sculpture Park extends across the Brooklyn campus and includes more than 70 sculptures, with works on loan, commissioned, and periodically changing.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor viewing conditions and individual works can change; consult Pratt’s current Sculpture Park Guide.

cards.entity_name: The Rubelle and Norman Schafler Gallery
cards.title: The Rubelle and Norman Schafler Gallery
cards.subtitle: Chemistry Building, first floor
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition, then spend time with work by Pratt students, faculty, and alumni rather than rushing through the room.
cards.short_summary: A Chemistry Building gallery for cross-disciplinary contemporary exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says the Schafler Gallery presents exhibitions by faculty, students, and alumni across departments and serves as a forum for contemporary culture.
cards.source_title: The Rubelle and Norman Schafler Gallery — Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: Pratt lists gallery hours, but exhibitions and access may change; verify the current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Steuben Gallery
cards.subtitle: Steuben Hall, Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Look up the current exhibition before heading over; this is a focused stop for viewing work by Pratt’s art community.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery that supports student, faculty, and alumni exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt states that Steuben Gallery supports exhibitions by students, faculty, and alumni during the year, including BFA thesis exhibitions.
cards.source_title: The Steuben Gallery — Pratt Institute School of Art
cards.access_notes: Exhibition schedules vary by semester; check Pratt’s current events calendar before visiting.

cards.title: ARC Building Photography Gallery
cards.subtitle: ARC Building lower level, 200 Willoughby Avenue
cards.notes: Time a visit around a listed photography show and use the lower-level gallery as a close look at graduating students’ displayed work.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level ARC gallery used for photography thesis exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s event page identifies the Photography Gallery in the ARC lower level and describes it as a venue for Photography BFA thesis shows within Pratt Shows.
cards.source_title: Pratt Shows: Photography BFA Thesis, Show 8 — Pratt Institute
cards.access_notes: The cited show has ended; consult Pratt’s current events calendar for the next exhibition and access details.

cards.title: Alumni Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Brooklyn Campus Library, 200 Willoughby Avenue
cards.notes: Watch for a listed talk, reading, or town hall and arrive with a question; the room is used as a library event space.
cards.short_summary: A library room used for campus talks, readings, and other events.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s Libraries history identifies the former Library Museum room as today’s Alumni Reading Room, used as an event space; Pratt also lists current events there.
cards.source_title: The Library Museum — Pratt Institute Libraries Special Collections
cards.access_notes: This is an event space, not a guaranteed drop-in study room; check Pratt’s events calendar and library guidance.

cards.title: Interfaith Commons
cards.subtitle: East Hall Annex, under the Pratt Chapel sign
cards.notes: Use this nondenominational room for quiet reflection or prayer, and bring or borrow the appropriate materials for your practice.
cards.short_summary: A daily-open, nondenominational reflection space in East Hall Annex.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt says the Interfaith Commons is a nondenominational space in the East Hall Annex, open daily for quiet reflection and prayer, with inclusive amenities and resources.
cards.access_notes: Pratt describes the space as open daily; confirm any program-related changes with Campus Ministry before visiting.

cards.title: Materials Lab
cards.subtitle: Pratt Brooklyn campus
cards.notes: Use the materials resources to compare objects and surfaces while developing a project; follow any lab-specific guidance before handling collections.
cards.short_summary: A Pratt lab for hands-on material exploration and research.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt lists the Materials Lab among spaces where students can interact with collections of objects and materials and research ways of making.
cards.access_notes: Lab access, orientations, and handling rules may be program-specific; verify current requirements with Pratt.

cards.title: Cannon Plaza
cards.subtitle: Brooklyn campus green space
cards.notes: Use the official map to locate this named outdoor plaza, then make it a legible meeting point while moving between nearby campus buildings.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor plaza shown on Pratt’s current Brooklyn campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt’s current Brooklyn campus map identifies Cannon Plaza among the campus’s green and open spaces.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus location; use Pratt’s current map and follow posted campus-access guidance.
